text:
Predicates:
RankedHigh(x) ::: x is ranked highly by the Women's Tennis Association.
ActivePlayer(x) ::: x is one of the most active players in major tennis.
LostTo(x, y) ::: x lost to y.
Player(x) ::: x is a tennis player.
Female(x) ::: x is a female tennis player.
Male(x) ::: x is a male tennis player.
AtRolandGarros2022(x) ::: x participated at Roland Garros 2022.
Published in 1946, Miroslav Venhoda wrote a book titled Method of Studying Gregorian Chant.

Premises:
∀x (RankedHigh(x) → ActivePlayer(x)) ::: Anyone ranked highly is among the most active players.
∀x (LostTo(x, IgaŚwiątek) → RankedHigh(x)) ::: Everyone who lost to Iga Świątek is ranked highly.
∀x (AtRolandGarros2022(x) ∧ Female(x) → LostTo(x, IgaŚwiątek)) ::: All female players at Roland Garros 2022 lost to Iga Świątek.
∀x (AtRolandGarros2022(x) → (Female(x) ∨ Male(x))) ::: All players at Roland Garros 2022 are either female or male.
∀x (Male(x) ∧ AtRolandGarros2022(x) → LostTo(x, RafaelNadal)) ::: All male players at Roland Garros 2022 lost to Rafael Nadal.
( (RankedHigh(CocoGauff) ∨ LostTo(CocoGauff, RafaelNadal)) → ¬Male(CocoGauff) ) ::: If Coco Gauff is either ranked highly or lost to Rafael Nadal, then Coco Gauff is not male.
CocoGauff at RolandGarros2022.

Conclusion:
¬(LostTo(CocoGauff, IgaŚwiątek) ∧ ActivePlayer(CocoGauff)) ::: Coco Gauff is not both a player who lost to Iga Świątek and one of the most active players in major tennis.
